item.title: The ANTECHAMBER: SCP seeking Greenlight: Re: The ANTECHAMBER: SCP seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for reviewing my concept. I was aware that a few SCPs dealt with Christian-like concepts of Hell, though I had not seen SCP-4661 or Arcadia.

My plan was to use a detached, clinical tone in Containment Procedures and Description, and then to use a slightly more narrative, direct style in a string of Exploration Logs, Interviews, and Incident Reports.

The SCP would include descriptions of how MTFs dealt with manifesting demons (I was being facetious with the "badass demon-killing"), as well as researchers' notes on these entities. But the main focus would be on the people exploring "Hell" (the Foundation would refer to it as the Abyss.)

Over several interview logs, the Mediums who access the SCP would try to explain what they see. The Mediums, who are of several faiths: Christian, Jewish, Islamic, Hindu, Buddhist; would experience the Abyss in different ways, since it is a metaphysical reality, and the human mind often needs to visualize and familiarize abstract concepts. What the Mediums see is often dark and traumatic, and repeated visits to the Abyss often eat away at their mental health.

Interviewing researchers do find a common theme among the Mediums' varying accounts: the horror of the Abyss is self-imposed. More than a simple torture chamber, the souls and entities within are locked in personal reveries, tortured by their own insanity, loneliness, and self-hatred as they constantly relive horrific fantasies and tear each other apart.

I agree that disturbing visuals alone can't carry an article. The central horror in this article is conceptual; existential. The visuals serve to fully realize that; to turn the scary idea into a tangible nightmare.

I had intended for the SCP itself: the Portals, Virgil Events, and such, to be rather mysterious. Mediums always experience some kind of Lobby or Antechamber. This room is manned by a figure in a white mask, (dubbed SCP-XXXX-A) who guides the visitor to the soul they ask for, and/or lets them explore Hell, but never explains itself. I would be happy to go more into this part of the SCP if you think that would improve the article.

As for the Chaos Insurgency, I only mention it once. A dead spy who had information the Foundation needed was a good motive for it to start using this SCP. Is there a problem in using the Insurgency?

P.S.: Is MTF Psi-8 "Silencers" the right group for this SCP?

item.title: Return to Monke - Greenlight Request / Review: Re: Return to Monke - Greenlight Request / Review
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look. I'll admit that the first few sentences of the description make me think of SCP-1836 (Mother in the Ice), only this is kind of a less interesting version because 1836 incorporates the legendary figure Sedna. This iceberg just kind of… seemingly exists in a strangely specific way for no reason.

Over the course of the article, a journal is found from a monkey

This just seems too conveniently story-wise. A lot of readers these days tend to be skeptical of the "wow look how nice that someone left a document that explains everything and also spoonfeeds story exposition too!" approach; if you really want to have the majority of the information about the item come from the documentation, a tale or GoI-format document may be a better approach. Otherwise the Foundation involvement seems like an afterthought, which wouldn't make sense for an SCP article about something seemingly so grandiose in terms of human implications.

who was bestowed intelligence by the Avatar of the Earth. Our monkey scientist then grapples with the stupidity of mankind,

I'm confused as to why the monkey scientist is so immediately dismissive of humans. We've got stuff like cloud seeding, painkillers, the internet… it also seems rather hypocritical to just see humans as a whole as "stupid" given that there are plenty of intelligent and good-hearted people out there.

before realizing that the only way to protect what gave him the ground to stand on, is to pack everything away and create a failsafe, so that Earth may live on.

I'm not sure what this means. What is the failsafe? What is being packed away? And if the monkey thinks humans are so stupid, why bother writing a journal that humans can understand?

Sorry, but I don't see this being workable at its current stage because all the individual elements seem kind of haphazardly smashed together rather than being thematically related in the context of the story. How is an iceberg related to turning people into monkeys, and how is that related to some random scientist dishing out their hot take on humanity? Why are shrines with feeling-language needed at all in this story?

item.title: SCP Idea: The Necro-Matriarch Broadcast Manifestations: Re: SCP Idea: The Necro-Matriarch Broadcast Manifestations
item.content:encoded:
For the ones who have a bad memory, no matter how severe it is, that same "grandma" will be completely different.

As for the language barrier problem, It will be no worry since the anomaly would be able to speak their language at ease, due to you know, them having an innate knowledge of the subject's past and current life.

Yeah, both of these make me as a reader skeptical because it just makes the anomaly too perfect and helpful, which comes off more as artificial and disingenuous to me as a reader rather than heartwarming.

+ show block
– hide block

I am sorry, I didn’t quite catch that. Could you please elaborate it?

What is the reason in the Foundation universe world for the radio to do what it does? Did someone make it because they wanted to talk to their grandma? Is a ghost grandma living in the radiowaves to haunt them? Some other reason?

I am planning to make “convenient online post” to be like the debut of the anomaly in the Foundation’s eyes

My point is that this is a kind of boring initial investigation setup.

Almost as if the mysterious creator of this anomaly is trying to play games with the Foundation, and benefit them at the same time.

Why would the creator want to play games with the Foundation?

On a unrelated note, do antique radios still function normally like they do, because I thought they were just for display.

I'm not familiar with antique radios. Although, if it only affects such radios, would there really be that many people who would be affected by such an anomaly, to the point where the Foundation would have enough cases to notice?

I only written the increased percentage in the draft, in about 35.5 percent.

I'm not sure a qualitative value like "morale" would be readily quantifiable or understandable when presented as a percentage. I recommend just sticking to similarly qualitative descriptions. There's no need to force a random percentage into the writing, especially given that readers will interpret percentages differently (one person might think 35.5 is a lot statistically, another person might think it's a number too small to be worth mentioning in a report).

The last thing you said is also great for a possible Tale about this skip

I personally am not convinced you'd be able to make a tale for this—the material I've mentioned would make more sense for a log or supplement page. Focus on writing an SCP article first.

item.title: The Hinterland Division (How many apocalypses could there be?): Re: The Hinterland Division (How many apocalypses could there be?)
item.content:encoded: Okay so let me try to explain it a little bit better since my original post was kind of vague. The division technically already existed and has been a key part of the foundation since not long after the Foundations conception, and has already eliminated several threats. The foundation isn’t really making a new division this is just a story behind the creation of the newest iteration of its leader. The reason that the other divisions of the foundation are not sufficient at it is because the threats that the division is made to stop are those that require entire knowledge of the foundation and it’s recourses , regardless of the security needed to have that information. The main idea of the story is very much inspired by the book Enders Game, I’m not sure if you’ve read it. The idea is that the existing Hinterland division is failing because it has not had someone fulfilling the position of the leader and strategist in years, as no good candidates have been found, and without someone that has the prowess to spearhead the division the researchers and members in the division are struggling to do it. The agent that the O5 chooses is purposefully trained and manipulated into being the best possible person to continue the work of the division. This story isn’t really meant to create a new part of the foundation but to explore an existing part of it that has been in my head for a really long time but is not included in any records due to the importance of its mission making its secrecy extremely important as well. I really want to shed some light and provide a look into what’s behind the curtain of the foundation since once you reach the level of the O5 and their staff everything gets rather hazy. The main character is of course the most explored and shown character but he also has several people he knows within the foundation, and I plan to actually develop the character at least partially of one of the O5 members, the one that is currently fulfilling the role of O5-13. There are going to be tales that show characters a low in the foundation of D class personnel in all of this as well. Of course I’m probably not going to write everything about this idea I’m coming up with as this is technically part of an even larger story about how the foundation has been changing and events within it over the years, this is just my version of a snippet of the mysteries in the ever mysterious organization.

item.title: SCP IDEA: "Home": Re: SCP IDEA: "Home"
item.content:encoded:
Sorry about the wait,

I didn't intend to make it sound like the village had ties to the Sarkic Cults. I meant that the SCP Foundation thought that the village had ties to the Sarkic Cults because of the flesh creatures. The members of the village, before anyone enters, are featureless flesh like creatures. There are animals that roam around the village that are also featureless. Once someone enters the village, the animals will resemble animals familiar to the person, such as their childhood dog.

I've decided that the village used to be a commune that a person stumbled upon one day. The commune was dwindling on supplies but tried to hide that fact. The person joins the commune after a while and feels at home. One day, the members of the commune attacked him, burned him, and ate him. They were planning on doing this the whole time and they gave him a false sense of home. This person was somehow anomalous and didn't know it, their soul combined with the village and terrorized the people living in it. The village now wants to bring the same fate to all who come across it in a fit of rage. It plays off of nostalgia because it has decided thats the best way to make people feel at home.
